title: One Evidenced Win, One Rejected Fake
objective: Record a bottleneck hypothesis before changing code, ship one change that moves p95 or SLO-meeting RPS on the identical workload, document a second change that did not help, and revalidate correctness.
whyThisMatters: The software-engineering performance task combines measure, profile, fix, and reject-a-fake-opt in one 18-hour pass. You already have a harness, profiles, traces, a cache experiment, query plans, a knee, and a capacity note. This close asks for judgment: one win you can defend with before/after numbers, and one apparent win you refuse to ship.
evidence: A hypothesis file committed before the optimization diff, naming the bottleneck and the metric you expect to move
Before and after results from the identical pe1t1-001 or pe1t1-006 command, each quoting p95 or SLO-meeting RPS
A shipped-change note stating the metric delta as a number and pointing at the profile, trace, or EXPLAIN evidence that justified the change
A rejected-change note with before/after numbers showing no improvement or a regression, and confirmation the change is not on the default path
A correctness test or invariant check shown passing after the shipped change
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The hypothesis file is committed before the first optimization commit and names one bottleneck plus one metric (p95 or SLO-meeting RPS).
Before and after runs use the same documented command; both results quote p95 or SLO-meeting RPS as numbers.
The shipped change moves that metric in the intended direction; the delta is computed from the two runs.
A second change has committed before/after numbers showing no gain or a regression and is absent from the default path.
A correctness test or recorded invariant is shown passing after the shipped change.
